question: A car starts from rest is accelerated to a velocity of 60 km/hr in 5 minutes. What is the acceleration of the car?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.055 m/s2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The initial velocity of the car is **0 m/s** because it starts from **rest**. ***Hence, u = 0.***
 
• The final velocity (v) is given as **60 km/hr**. To find the acceleration in **m/s2**, we must convert the units to the **SI system**.
 
• The conversion of **60 km/hr** to **m/s** is calculated by multiplying it by **5/18**. Therefore, **v = 60 x (5/18) = 16.67 m/s**.
 
• The time (t) taken is **5 minutes**. This must also be converted into **seconds** for consistency. Since **1 minute = 60 seconds**, the total time is **5 x 60 = 300 seconds**.
 
• Acceleration (a) is defined by the formula **a = (v - u) / t**. Plugging in the values: **a = (16.67 - 0) / 300**.
 
• Performing the calculation: **16.67 / 300** results in **0.0555... m/s2**. Rounding this value gives the acceleration as **0.055 m/s2**. ***Hence, the calculated value matches the first option.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration:** It is a **vector quantity** that represents the rate at which an object changes its **velocity**. An object is accelerating if its speed or direction changes.
 
• **Equations of Motion:** These equations, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton**, describe the relationship between velocity, acceleration, displacement, and time. The first equation is **v = u + at**.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** This occurs when the **velocity** of an object changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**. A car speeding up steadily on a straight road is an example of **linear acceleration**.
 
• **Retardation:** If the final velocity is less than the initial velocity, the acceleration is **negative**. This is commonly referred to as **deceleration** or **retardation**.
 
• **SI Units:** The Standard International unit for **velocity** is **m/s** (meters per second) and for **acceleration** is **m/s2** (meters per second squared).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply the value by **5/18**. Conversely, to convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by **18/5**.
 
• **Time Conversion:** Always ensure time is in **seconds** when calculating **acceleration** in **m/s2**. **1 hour = 3600 seconds**.
 
• **Zero Velocity:** Whenever a problem states that an object "starts from **rest**", the **initial velocity (u)** is always **0**. If an object "comes to a **stop**", the **final velocity (v)** is **0**.
 
• **Magnitude and Direction:** Since acceleration is a **vector**, it is defined by both **magnitude** (e.g., **0.055**) and **direction**. In this problem, the magnitude is requested.
